questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Quiescent centre is the zone of :
options: least mitotic activity in the root apex
least mitotic activity in the shoot apex
maximum mitotic activity in the root apex
maximum mitotic activity in the shoot apex
questions.solution: Quiescent centre is an area at the top of the root apical meristem where the cells have least mitotic activity i.e., the rate of cell division is lower than in surrounding tissue.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: 'Sea fan' belongs to :
questions.solution: Sea fan is common name of Gorgonia. It belongs to phylum-Coelenterata, class-Anthozoa and order-Gorgonacea.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Trochophore is the larva of :
questions.solution: Trochophore is cilliated, larval stage of polychaetes, mollsucs and rotifers. Neopilina, Chiton and Pila belong to phylum-Molusca. Molluscan development is either direct or with metamorphosis through the trochophore stage.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Food storage in Leucosolenia occur by :
questions.solution: Food storage in Leucosolenia occurs by thesocyte. Thesocytes have lobose pseudopodia and are filled with food reserves, thus, acting as storage cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Class Crustacea differs from Insecta in having :
questions.solution:
The main characteristics of class Crustacea and Insecta are as follows :
(1) Class Crustacea : Mostly aquatic with gills, two pairs of antennae and atleast three pairs of jaws, appendages mostly biramous and always more than four in the trunk region.
Example : prawn, crab, lobster etc.
(2) Class Insecta : Hexapod arthropods with a pair of antennae and three pairs of Jaws.
Example : cockroach, grasshopper, bees, housefly etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following character is present essentialy in chordates ?
options: Blood flow in forward direction in ventral blood vessels
questions.solution:
Chordate animals, at some time in their life history, exhibit the following three diagnostic charcters :
(1) Presence of notochord.
(2) Presence of dorsal tubular nerve cord.
(3) Presence of gill clefts during development.
Beside these, some other characters are :
(4) Ventral heart.
(5) Hepatic portal system.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which insect is useful for us?
questions.solution: Bombyx mori is a silk producing insect, which is reared on mulberry leaves for commercial production of silk whereas mosquito, Musca and Periplanata are harmful arthropodes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A nucleotide is a molecule consisting of a :
questions.solution:
A nucleotide is a nucleoside (sugar + nitorgen base) with phosphate group.
Thus, nucleoside $=$ sugar + nitrogenous base nucleotide $=$ nucleoside + phosphate group

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Non-protein part of enzyme is known as :
questions.solution:
The enzyme complex (holoenzyme) is made up of two parts i.e., protein part (apoenzyme) and non-protein part (cofactor). Cofactor is of three types -
(i) prosthetic group
(ii) coenzymes
(iii) metal ions
Holoenzymes $=$ Apoenzyme + Prosthetic group (Enzyme complex) (Protein part) (Non-protein part).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In DNA, which is absent?
questions.solution: Uracil remains absent in DNA. It is present in RNA. The nitrogen bases of DNA and RNA are as follows :

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cell membrane in animals is composed mainly of the molecule of :
questions.solution: Chemically, the plasma membrane or cell membrane is made up of $60 \%$ proteins and $40 \%$ lipids. The percentage of carbohydrates ranges from 1-10 which are in the form of glycoproteins or glycolipids. Proteins may be extrinsic (peripheral) and intrinsic (integral) while lipids may be phospholipids, glycolipids and sterols.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one is single membrane cell organelle?
questions.solution: Endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria and chloroplast are double membraned cell organelles whereas lysosome is a single membraned cell organelle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pigment anthocyanin is located in :
questions.solution: Vacuoles are the storage depots of cells, surrounded by a single membrane. They contain excess water, waste products, mineral elements, cell sap and sometimes a soluble pigment anthocyanin also.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cell theory was propounded in 1838-39 by :
questions.solution: The cell theory or cell doctrine is credited to Matthias Schleiden (1838) a botanist of Germany and Theodor Schwann (1839), a zoologist also of Germany.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Green plants constitute :
questions.solution: Green plants constitute the first trophic level at these store energy by trapping the light and forming the food through photosynthesis and then passed to other organisms from the plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Carrier of fluorosis is :
questions.solution: Fluorosis is a disease caused by the consumption of water with excess fluoride or fluorine.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Insects captured by insectivorous plants fulfil their requirements of
questions.solution: The insectivorous plants grow in nitrogen deficient soil and their nitrogen requirement is fulfilled by capturing and digesting the insects.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Hydroponics is a :
questions.solution: Hydroponics refers to soil-less cultures of plants and growing them on mineral solution.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The enzyme responsible for atmospheric nitrogen fixation is :
questions.solution:
Enzyme nitrogenase plays a key role in $\mathrm{N}_2$ fixations and remains active only during anaerobic condition. It is made up of two protein subunits :
(i) non-heme iron protein or Fe-protein or dinitrogen reductase.
(ii) Iron molybdenum protein or Mo-Fe protein or dinitrogenase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is non symbiotic bio-fertilizer?
questions.solution:
1. Azotobacter is a non-symbiotic, free-living nitrogen-fixing bacteria.
2. They are aerobic and free-living soil microbes, which perform an essential function in the nitrogen cycle.
3. They convert atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia, which is further utilized by plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Micro-nutrients are :
options: less important in nutrition than macronutrients
as important in nutrition as macro-nutrients
may be omitted from culture media without any detrimental effect on the plant
called micro because they play only minor role in nutrition
questions.solution: Micro-nutrients are the minerals/elements which are required in less amount by the plants and thus are present in less quantity in the plants but these are as important as the macro-nutrients. Examples of micro-nutrients iron ( Fe ), manganese ( Mn ), copper $(\mathrm{Cu})$, zinc $(\mathrm{Zn})$, molybdenum (Mo), boron (B) and chlorine (Cl).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Floral formula of is characteristic of the family :
questions.solution: The member of sub-family Caesal pinieae have bracteate, zygomorphic, bisexual, hypogynous, pentamerous flowers with 5 -sepals (polysepalous) 5-petals (polypeptalous), $5+5$ stamens (polyandrous) and monocarpellary, superior ovary with marginal placentation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The number of female flowers found in a cyanthium is :
questions.solution: Cyanthium is a special type of inflorescence (found in Euphorbia sp.) with a cup shaped involucre having nector secreting glands, a centrally placed single large female flower which is reduced to pistil surrounded by many male flowers present in the form of stamens.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The plant that is characteristics component of mangrove vegetation :
questions.solution: Rhizophora mangel is the component of mangrove vegetation and grows in marshes or nitrogen and air deficient soil. These plants possess vivipary and pneumatophores or respiratory roots.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In turnip, $2 / 3$ part of swollen area is derived from :
questions.solution: In turnip, napiform root is found, the swollen part of which is derived from the hypocotyl.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The law of limiting factors for photosynthesis was enunciated by :
questions.solution: Blackman (1905) proposed the law of limiting factor according to which, "when a biological process is controlled as to its rapidity by a number of separate factors, the rate of the process is limited by the pace of the slowest factor.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The light phase of photosynthesis is called :
questions.solution: Hill reaction, also called as light reaction is a photochemical reaction. In this, reduced enzymes and phosphate bond energy (ATP) are produced.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The plant Cuscuta shows maximum photosynthesis in :
questions.solution: Cuscuta is a parasitic plant which gets prepared food from other plants through the haustoria. At this plant lacks chlorophyll, it is unable to perform photosynthesis or to make its own food itself.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Gibberellin was first extracted from :
questions.solution: Yabuta and Hayashi (1939) isolated an active substance from a fungus, Gibberella fujikuroi and called it gibberellin-A. It causes backane disease in rice seedlings.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following as a living fossil ?
questions.solution: Linkgo, a member of order linkgoales, is called living fossil because all the others except Ginko biloba are now extinct.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The amphibians of plant kingdom are :
questions.solution: The bryophytes are terrestrial plants, generally growing in moist and shady places but always need water for fertilization. Hence, these are called amphibians of the plant kingdom.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The alga used for quick sewage disposal is :
questions.solution: Certain algae such as Chlorella, Chlamydomonas, Scenedesmus, Oscillatoria etc., are used for the quick disposal of sewage, domestic and some industrial wastes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The protein rich alga is :
questions.solution: Chlorella, commonly known as space alga is a protein rich alga, containing about $50 \%$ protein, $20 \%$ lipids, $20 \%$ carbohydrates and a little percentage of vitamin- $\mathrm{B}_2, \mathrm{~B}_{12}, \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{H}, \mathrm{K}$ etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The incomplete breakdown of sugars in anaerobic respiration results in the formation of :
questions.solution: The anaerobic respiration occurs in many bacteria, some fungi, germinating seeds and some fruits. It involves the incomplete breakdown of sugars forming $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{OH}$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ as end products and 27 kcal energy is released.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During anaerobic conditions, the rate of glycolysis increases, is called :
questions.solution: Pasteur's effect refers to the increase of rate of glycolysis in absence of $\mathrm{O}_2$ due to the non-availability of those enzymes which are easily available in the presence of $\mathrm{O}_2$.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: How many ATP are formed by oxidation of one glucose molecule in liver cells ?
questions.solution:
In liver cells and prokaryotic cells, 38 ATP are produced by the complete oxidation of one molecule of glucose.
$\begin{aligned} \text { Glycolysis } 2 \text { ATP directly } & =2 \text { ATP } \\ 2 \text { mol. of NADH } & =6 \text { ATP }\end{aligned}$
Pyruvic acid to
Acetyl Co-A 2 mol. of NADH = 6 ATP
Citric acid 6 mol. of NADH = 18 ATP
  cycle
$\begin{array}{ll}2 \mathrm{~mol} . \text { of FADH } & =4 \mathrm{ATP} \\ 2 \mathrm{~mol} . \text { of GTP } & =2 \mathrm{ATP} \\ \text { Total } & =38 \mathrm{ATP}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Perisperm is :
questions.solution: Perisperm is the remnant of nucellus. It is found in Piperaceae and Scitaminaceae. It is formed when the nucellus is not completely used up and is present in the form of a thin layer in the seed enclosing the embryo and the endosperm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: An orthotropus ovule is one in which micropyle and chalaza are :
questions.solution: Orthotropous ovule is also called atropous. In this type of ovule the micropyle, chalaza and funicle lie in one straight line, e.g., Polygonaceae, Piperaceae etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Transpiration would be lowest when :
options: enough water is in the soil
questions.solution: When atmospheric RH is high, the temperature of atmosphere will be low. This will reduce the rate of evaporation and also reduces the rate of transpiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Who said that "transpiration is a necessary evil" ?
questions.solution: Curtis (1926) called transpiration as necessary evil because it provides some beneficial aspects but on the other hand, many functioning and energy gets wasted from absorption of water upto the stage of transpiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following exhibits a direct porportionality to transpiration?
questions.solution: Temperature and wind have the direct proportional to the transpiration. When the winds faster and dry and temperature is high, the rate of water evaporation will also high, increasing the rate of transpiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Water in plants is transported by :
questions.solution: The water absorbed by root hairs is transported to other parts of the plant through xylem. Phloem transfers food prepared in leaves to the other parts. Cambium is responsible for secondary growth while epidermis is the outermost protective layer of cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The most important force which pulls water up in tall trees is :
questions.solution: ive (inter-molecular) force between $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ molecules. It also helps in maintaining the continuity of water column in tall trees.

treating ethyl alcohol with excess of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ at $430-440 \mathrm{~K}$

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.solution: The structure of glycine is as So, it is optically inactive.

questions.subject: Chemistry

options: gives silver mirror with Tollen's reagent
questions.solution: Glucose gives silver mirror with Tollen's reagent while fructose does not.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $A+B \rightleftharpoons C+D$. If initially the concentration of $A$ and $B$ are both equal but at equilibrium, concentration of $D$ will be twice of that of $A$, then what will be the equilibrium constant of reaction?
questions.solution: $K_c=\frac{[C][D]}{[A][B]}=\frac{2 x \times 2 x}{x \times x}=4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The half-life of a first order reaction having rate constant $k=1.7 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ is :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & k=1.7 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~s}^{-1} \\ & t_{1 / 2}=\frac{0.693}{k}=\frac{0.693}{1.7 \times 10^{-5}}=11.3 \mathrm{~h}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aspirin is :
questions.solution: Aspirin is used as antipyretic as well as analgesic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following have highest electron affinity ?
questions.solution: Electron affinity of halogens is maximum in a period and it decreases in a group from top to bottom but the EA of chlorine is greater than fluorine due to smaller atomic size of fluorine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The geometry of $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4$ and $\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{PPh}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2$ are :
questions.solution: $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4$ and $\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{PPh}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2$ are tetrahedral in geometrical shape, because co-ordination number of Ni is 4 in both cases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following have maximum number of unpaired electrons?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} \longrightarrow[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^5 4 s^0$
Number of unpaired electrons $=5$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What amount of $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ gas liberated at anode, if 1 ampere current is passed for 30 minute from NaCl solution?
questions.solution:
$2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \rightarrow \underset{1 \text { mole }}{\mathrm{Cl}_2}+\underset{2 \times 96500 \text { coulomb }}{2 e^{-} \text {(At anode) }}\begin{aligned} Q & =i t=1 \times 30 \times 60 \\ & =1800 \text { coulomb }\end{aligned}$
The amount of chlorine liberated by passing 1800 coulomb of electric charge
$=\frac{1 \times 1800 \times 71}{2 \times 96500}=0.66 \mathrm{~g}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is secondary pollutant?
questions.solution: Pollutants which are formed by reaction amongst the primary pollutants (persist in the environment in the form they are passed into it) are called as secondary pollutants e.g., peroxyacyl nitrates (PAN) are formed through reaction between nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons in the presence of sunlight.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hardness of water is due to presence of salts of :
questions.solution: Hardness of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is due to the presence of bicarbonates, chlorides, and sulphates of Ca and Mg ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Given pH of a solution $A$ is 3 and it is mixed with another solution $B$ having pH 2 . If both mixed, then resultant pH of the solution will be :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{pH} \text { of } A=3 \quad \mathrm{pH} \text { of } B=2 \\ & \therefore\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=10^{-3} \mathrm{M}, \quad\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=10^{-2} \mathrm{M} \\ & \text { Total }\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right] \\ & =10^{-3}+10^{-2}=10^{-3}+10 \times 10^{-3} \\ & =11 \times 10^{-3} \\ & \therefore \quad \mathrm{pH}=-\log _{10}\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=-\log \left(11 \times 10^{-3}\right) \\ & =3-\log 11 \\ & =3-1.04=1.96 \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is carborundum?
questions.solution: Reason being SiC is also used as carborundum.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is false ?
options: Diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon
Bleaching action of $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ in moist condition is not permanent
questions.solution: Reason being bleaching action of $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ in moist condition is permanent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is strongest acid?
questions.solution:
We know that acidic strength $\propto$ Oxidation number
$\therefore$ Correct order is
$\stackrel{+1}{\mathrm{HClO}} \lt \stackrel{+3}{\mathrm{HClO}_2} \lt \stackrel{+5}{\mathrm{HClO}}_3 \lt \stackrel{+7}{\mathrm{HClO}_4}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What will be the order of Ist ionisation energy ?
questions.solution: In a sub-group ionisation energy decreases from top to bottom because atomic size increases. So, the Ist IE of $\mathrm{Li}, \mathrm{Na}$ and K are in the order $\mathrm{Li}\gt\mathrm{Na}\gt\mathrm{K}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the formula of bleaching powder ?
questions.solution: Bleaching powder is represented by the formula $\mathrm{Ca}(\mathrm{OCl}) \mathrm{Cl}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When electrons are trapped into the crystal in anion vacancy, the defect is known as :
questions.solution: F-centres are the sites where anions are missing and instead electrons are present. They are responsible for colour.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Certain crystals produce electric signals on application of perssure. This phenomenon is called :
questions.solution: Certain crystals produce electric signals on application of pressure. This phenomenon is called piezoelectricity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not a property of liquid state?
options: Intermolecular force of attraction in a liquid is quite large
All liquids accompanied by cooling on evaporation
Lower the boiling point of a liquid, greater is its vapour pressure at room temperature
A liquid boils at high temperature at the top of a mountain than at the sea level
questions.solution: We know that boiling point falls on decreasing the pressure. At mountain air pressure is low so liquid boils at lower temperature at the top of mountain than at the sea level.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If for a sucrose solution, elevation in boiling point is $0.1^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, then what will be the boiling point of NaCl solution for same molal concentration?
questions.solution:
Elevation in boiling point is a colligative property as it depends upon the number of particles.
$\Delta T_b \propto n$
For sucrose, $n=1, \Delta T_b=0.1^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
For $\mathrm{NaCl}, n=2, \Delta T_b=0.2^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Total number of atoms represented by the compound $\mathrm{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is :
questions.solution: Total number of atoms in $\mathrm{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is 21 .

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A certain sample of gas has a volume of 0.2 L measured at 1 atm pressure and $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. At the same pressure but $273^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, its volume will be :
questions.solution:
According to Charles' law
$\begin{array}{rlrl}\frac{V_1}{T_1} & =\frac{V_2}{T_2} \\ & \frac{0.2}{273} & =\frac{V_2}{476} \\ \therefore \quad & V_2 & =0.4 \mathrm{~L}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The entropy values (in $\mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ ) of $\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g})=130.6, \quad \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{~g})=223.0 \quad$ and $\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})=186.7$ at 298 K and 1 atm pressure. Then entropy change for the reaction :
$\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})$ is :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \Delta S^{\circ} & =2 S^{\circ}{ }_{\mathrm{HCl}}-\left(S_{\mathrm{H}_2}^{\circ}+S^{\circ}{ }_{\mathrm{Cl}_2}\right) \\ & =2 \times 186.7-(130.6+223.0) \\ & =19.8 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The enthalpy of combustion at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ of $\mathrm{H}_2$, cyclohexane $\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12}\right)$ and cyclohexene $\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{10}\right)$ are $-241,-3920$ and $-3800 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$ respectively. The heat of hydrogenation of cyclohexene is :
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{H}_2+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\ & \Delta H=-241 \mathrm{~kJ} . .\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{10}+\frac{17}{2} \mathrm{O}_2 \longrightarrow 6 \mathrm{CO}_2+5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\ \Delta H=-3800 \mathrm{~kJ} \ldots \text { (ii) }\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12}+9 \mathrm{O}_2 \longrightarrow & 6 \mathrm{CO}_2+6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\ & \Delta H=-3920 \mathrm{~kJ} \ldots \text { (iii) }\end{aligned}$
hydrogenation of cyclohexene-
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{10}+\mathrm{H}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12} \\ & \mathrm{Eq} \text { (i) } \begin{aligned} \mathrm{Eq} & \text { (ii) }-\mathrm{Eq} \text { (iii) } \\ \Delta H & =-241-3800-(-3920) \\ & =-4041+3920 \\ & =-121 \mathrm{~kJ}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a $L-C-R$ circuit, the capacitance is made one-fourth, then what should be change in inductance, so that the circuit remains in resonance?
questions.solution:
Resonance frequency $f=\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{L C}}$
For the circuit to remain in resonance, $\sqrt{L C}=$ constant
$\begin{aligned} or \quad L_1 C_1 & =L_2 C_2 \\ or \quad L C & =L_2 \frac{C}{4} \\ \therefore L_2 & =4 L\end{aligned}\therefore$ Inductance should be change to four times.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Radius of first Bohr orbit is $r$. What is the radius of 2 nd Bohr orbit?
questions.solution:
Radius of Bohr orbit
$\begin{array}{l} r \propto n^2 \\ \frac{r_1}{r_2} =\left(\frac{n_1}{n_2}\right)^2 \\ \Rightarrow \frac{r}{r_2} =\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 \\ \Rightarrow \frac{r}{r_2} =\frac{1}{4} \\ \Rightarrow r_2 =4 r .\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.q: Which of the following is not an inelastic collision?
options: A man jump on a cart
A bullet embedded in a block
questions.solution:
"Man jumping on cart" and "bullet imbedded in a block" are examples when two bodies have to move together after collision, therefore both of them are inelastic collision.
Where as it is not the case for "collision of two glass balls".

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform wire of length $l$ and having resistance $R$ is cut into $n$ equal parts and all parts are connected in parallel, then the equivalent resistance will be :
questions.solution:
Resistance of each part $R^{\prime}=\frac{R}{n}$
When, these parts are connected in parallel.
Then, $\frac{1}{R^{\prime \prime}}=\frac{1}{R^{\prime}}+\frac{1}{R^{\prime}} \ldots . n$ time
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{n}{R^{\prime}} \\ \therefore \quad R^{\prime \prime} & =\frac{R^{\prime}}{n}=\frac{R}{n^2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the given circuit, what will be the equivalent resistance between the points $A$ and $B$ ?
questions.solution:
$\because \quad \frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{6}\therefore$ Given, circuit is a balanced Wheatstone's Bridge.
So, $10 \Omega$ resistance will be ineffective. Equivalent resistance of upper arms
$R_1=2+3=5 \Omega\therefore$ Equivalent resistance of lower arms
$\begin{aligned} R_2 & =4+6=10 \Omega \\ R_{A B} & =\frac{R_1 R_2}{R_1+R_2} \\ & =\frac{5 \times 10}{5+10} \\ & =\frac{50}{10}=\frac{10}{3} \Omega\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The light rays having photons of energy 1.8 eV are falling on a metal surface having a work function $1 \cdot 2 \mathrm{eV}$. What is the stopping potential to be applied to stop the emitting electrons ?
questions.solution:
Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectron
$\begin{aligned} & (\mathrm{KE})_{\max }=E-\phi \\ & =1.8-1.2 \\ & =0.6 \mathrm{eV} \\ & \text { i.e., } \quad e V_0=(\mathrm{KE})_{\max } \\ & \text { or } \quad e V_0=0.6 \mathrm{eV} \\ & \end{aligned}\therefore$ Stopping potential $V_0=0.6 \mathrm{eV}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Who discovered X-rays ?
questions.solution: Wilhelm Roentgen was already working on the effects of cathode rays during 1895, before he actually discovered X-rays.His experiments involved the passing of electric current through gases at extremely low pressure.So,the answer is option 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two similar charges having mass $m$ and $2 m$ are placed in an electric field. The ratio of their kinetic energy is :
questions.solution:
Force on charged particle is electric field
$F=q E\therefore$ Acceleration $a=\frac{F}{m}=\frac{q E}{m}\therefore$ Velocity
$\begin{aligned} v & =u+a t \\ & =0+\frac{q E}{m} t\end{aligned}$
So, kinetic energy
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{\frac{1}{2} m_1\left(\frac{q E}{m_1} t\right)^2}{\frac{1}{2} m_2\left(\frac{q E}{m_2} t\right)^2} \\ & =\frac{m_2}{m_1}=\frac{2 m}{m} \\ & =\frac{2}{1} \\ & =2: 1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charge $Q$ is distributed uniformly in a sphere (solid). Then, the electric field at any point $r$, where, $r \lt R$ ( $r$ is the radius of sphere) varies as :
questions.solution: . Electric field intensity at a point inside the sphere $\quad E=\frac{Q}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 R} r\therefore \quad E \propto r$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two equal -ve charges $-q$ are fixed at the point $(0, a)$ and $(0, -a)$ on the $y$-axis. A positive charge $Q$ is released from rest at the poin $(2 a, 0)$ on the $x$-axis. The charge will :
options: move to the origin and remain at rest
questions.solution: Component of force on charge $+Q$ at $P$, along $x$-axis, $\begin{aligned} F_x & =\frac{2 Q q}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0\left(a^2+x^2\right)} \cos \theta \\ & =\frac{2 Q q}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0\left(a^2+x^2\right)} \times \frac{x}{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}} \\ & =\frac{2 Q q x}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0\left(a^2+x^2\right)^{3 / 2}}\end{aligned}$ Which is not directly proportional to $x$. So, motion is oscillatory but not SHM.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two planets are revolving around the earth with velocities $v_1$ and $v_2$ and in radii $r_1$ and $r_2\left(r_1 \gt r_2\right)$ respectively. Then:
questions.solution:
Orbital velocity $v=\sqrt{g r}\frac{v_1}{v_2}=\sqrt{\frac{r_1}{r_2}}$
As, $r_1 \gt r_2$ so, $v_1 \gt v_2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Earth is revolving around the sun. If the distance of the earth from the sun is reduced to $1 / 4$ th of the present distance then the length of present day will be reduced by :
questions.solution:
From Kepler's law
$\begin{aligned} & T^2 \propto R^3 \\ & \therefore \quad\left(\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^2=\left(\frac{R_1}{R_2}\right)^3 \\ & \frac{T_1}{T_2}=\left(\frac{R_1}{R_2}\right)^{3 / 2}=\left(\frac{R}{R / 4}\right)^{3 / 2} \\ & =(4)^{3 / 2}=(2)^3=8 \\ & \therefore \quad T_2=\frac{T_1}{8} \\ & \end{aligned}$
Hence, the length of the day is reduced by $\frac{1}{8}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: There are two planets and the ratio of radius of the two planets is $K$ but ratio of acceleration due to gravity of both planets is $g$. What will be the ratio of their escape velocity?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} v_e & =\sqrt{R g} \\ \frac{v_1}{v_2} & =\sqrt{\frac{R_1}{R_2} \cdot \frac{g_1}{g_2}} \\ & =\sqrt{K g} \\ & =(K g)^{1 / 2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which is true for rolling friction $\left(\mu_r\right)$, static friction $\left(\mu_s\right)$ and kinetic friction $\left(\mu_k\right)$ :
questions.solution:
Static friction is always greater than kinetic friction, and rolling friction is less than kinetic friction, so
$\mu_s \gt \mu_k \gt \mu_r$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two weights $w_1$ and $w_2$ are suspended to the two strings on a frictionless pulley. When the pulley is pulled up with an acceleration $g$, then the tension in the string is :
questions.solution: Equation of motion for first weight $\begin{aligned} T-m_1 g & =m_1(g+a) \\ \Rightarrow \quad T-2 m_1 g & =m_1 a\ldots(1)\end{aligned}$ For second weight $\begin{aligned} m_2 g-T & =m_2(a-g) \\ 2 m_2 g-T & =m_2 a\ldots(2)\end{aligned}$ On solving Eqs. (1) and (2) $\begin{aligned} T & =\frac{4 m_1 m_2 g}{\left(m_1+m_2\right)} \\ & =\frac{4 w_1 w_2}{\left(w_1+w_2\right)}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a charge particle enters perpendiculary in the uniform magnetic field, then :
options: energy and momentum both remains constant
energy remains constant but momentum changes
energy changes but momentum remains constant
questions.solution: When charge particle enters in a magnetic field perpendicularly, then the magnitude of its velocity remains constant, but direction changes, so its energy (scalar quantity) remains constant, but its momentum (vector quantity) changes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car starts from rest, moves with an acceleration $a$ and then decelerates at a constant rate $b$ for sometimes to come to rest. If the total time taken is $t$. The maximum velocity of car is given by :
questions.solution:
Let car acceleates for time $t_1$ and decelerates for time $t_2$ then
$t_1+t_2=t$.....(1)
From
v=u+a t
$\begin{aligned} & v =u+a t_1 \\ \Rightarrow v & =a t_1\end{aligned}$
For deceleration
$\begin{aligned} & v=u-a t \\ & 0=a t_1-b t_2 (\because u=v)\\ & a t_1=b t_2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad t_2=\frac{a t_1}{b} \\ & \therefore \quad t_1+\frac{a t_1}{b}=1 [From Eq. (1)]\\ & \Rightarrow \quad t_1\left(1+\frac{a}{b}\right)=t \\ & \Rightarrow \quad t_1=\frac{b t}{a+b} \\ & \end{aligned}\therefore$ Maximum velocity of car
$v=a t_1=\frac{a b t}{a+b}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A river is flowing from west to east with a speed of $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{min}$. A man can swim in still water with a velocity $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{min}$. In which direction should the man swim so, as to take the shortest possible path to go to the south?
questions.solution: Let the swimmer swims at an angle $\theta$ with the vertical. $\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \sin \theta & =\frac{v_r}{v_s}=\frac{5}{10}=\frac{1}{2}=\sin 30^{\circ} \\ \theta & =30^{\circ}\end{aligned}$ The swimmer should swim $30^{\circ}$ east of south to take the shortest possible path to go to the south.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In the reaction given below
${ }_{86} A^{222} \longrightarrow{ }_{84} B^{210}$
how many $\alpha$ and $\beta$-particles are emitted?
questions.solution:
${ }_{86} A^{222} \longrightarrow{ }_{84} B^{210}\begin{aligned} \text { Decrease in mass number } & =222-210 \\ & =12\end{aligned}\therefore$ Number of $\alpha$-particles emitted
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{12}{4}=3 \\ { }_{86} A^{222} \longrightarrow{ }_{80} X^{210} & \longrightarrow 84 B^{210}\end{aligned}$
Increase in atomic number $=84-80=4\therefore$ Number of $\beta$-particles emitted $=4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The phenomenon of radioactivity is :
options: exothermic change which increases or decreases with temperature
nuclear process does not depend on external factors
questions.solution: Radioactivity is a natural process which does not depend upon external factors.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The element ${ }_{90} \mathrm{Th}^{232}$ belongs to thorium series. Which of the following will act as the end product of the series ?
questions.solution: The end product of thorium series is $\mathrm{Pb}-208$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pendulum is undergoing SHM with frequency $f$. What is the frequency of its kinetic energy ?
questions.solution: Let, $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{A} \sin \omega \mathrm{t}\mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{A} \omega \cos \omega \mathrm{t}$ Kinetic energy, $\mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m} \omega^2 \mathrm{~A}^2 \cos ^2 \omega \mathrm{t} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m} \omega^2 \mathrm{~A}^2\left(\frac{1+\cos 2 \omega \mathrm{t}}{2}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{4} \mathrm{~m} \omega^2 \mathrm{~A}^2\left(1+\cos ^2 \omega \mathrm{t}\right) \\ & \therefore \omega_{\mathrm{K}}=2 \omega\end{aligned}\therefore$ Frequency of oscillation of $\mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E}=2 \mathrm{f} \quad\left[\mathrm{f}=\frac{\omega}{2 \pi}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the length of a pendulum is made 9 times and mass of the bob is made 4 times, then the value of time period becomes :
questions.solution:
Time period $T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$
i.e., time period does not depend on the mass of the bob.
$\begin{aligned} \therefore & & T & \propto \sqrt{l} \\ & & \frac{T_1}{T_2} & =\sqrt{\frac{l_1}{l_2}} \\ & & \frac{T}{T_2} & =\sqrt{\frac{l}{9 l}} \\ & \therefore & T_2 & =3 T\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a convex lens of focal length 80 cm and a concave lens of focal length 50 cm are combined together, what will be their resultant power ?
questions.solution:
$f_1=+80 \mathrm{~cm}, f_2=-50 \mathrm{~cm}$.
Resultant focal length
$\begin{aligned} F & =\frac{f_1 f_2}{f_1+f_2} \\ & =\frac{80 \times-50}{80-50}=\frac{-4000}{30} \\ & =-\frac{4000}{3} \mathrm{~cm} .\end{aligned}$
Resultant power $\begin{aligned} P & =\frac{100}{F}=\frac{100}{-400 / 3} \\ & =-\frac{3}{4} \\ & =-0.75 \mathrm{D} .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The time taken by light to pass through 4 mm thick glass slab of refractive index 1.5 will be : (velocity of light in air $=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ )
questions.solution:
Time taken by light
$\begin{aligned} t & =\frac{\mu d}{c} \\ & =\frac{1.5 \times 4 \times 10^{-3}}{3 \times 10^8}=2 \times 10^{-11} \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A convex lens forms a full image of the object on a screen. If half of the lens is covered with an opaque object, then :
options: half of the image is seen
full image is seen and of same intensity
full image is seen and of decreased intensity
questions.solution: If half of the lens is covered with an opaque object, then, full image is seen but intensity of image decreases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
If the focal length of a lens of a camera is $5 f$ and that of another is $2.5 f$, what is the time of exposure for the second, if for the first one is $\frac{1}{200} \mathrm{~s}$ ?
(where $f$ is focal length/unit aperture)
questions.solution:
Ratio of time of expoiusers
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{t_1}{t_2}=\left(\frac{f_1}{f_2}\right)^2=\left(\frac{5 f}{2.5 f}\right)^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1 / 200}{t_2}=(2)^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad t_2=\frac{1}{800} \mathrm{~s} \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A lens acts as converging in air and diverging when immersed in water. Then, refractive index of lens is :
questions.solution: When lens is immersed in water then its nature changes. The refractive index of lens is less than that of wateri.e., less than 1.33 .

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plane glass slab is kept over various colour letters, the letter which appears least raised is :
questions.solution:
Refractive index
$\mu=\frac{\text { real depth }}{\text { apparent depth }}$
For red colour, refractive index is minimum, i.e., it will have maximum apparent depth and hence, appears least raised.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A light passing through air has wavelength $6000 Å$. The wavelength when same ray passes through a glass slab of refractive index 1.5 will be :
questions.solution:
When light ray passes through a glass slab, then new wavelength
$\begin{aligned} \lambda^{\prime} & =\frac{\lambda}{\mu}=\frac{6000}{1.5} \\ & =4000 Å\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angular momentum of a rotating body changes from $A_0$ to $4 A_0$ in 4 seconds. The torque acting on the body is :
questions.solution: Torque $\begin{aligned} \tau=\frac{d L}{d t} & =\frac{\left(4 A_0-A_0\right)}{4} \\ & =\frac{3 A_0}{4} .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a spherical ball rolls on a table without slipping the friction of its total energy associated with rotational energy is :
questions.solution:
Rotational energy of sphere
$E_R=\frac{1}{2} I \omega^2$
For sphere, moment of inertia
$\begin{aligned} I & =\frac{2}{5} m R^2 \\ \therefore \quad E_R & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{2}{5} m R^2\right)\left(\frac{v}{R}\right)^2 \\ & =\frac{1}{5} m v^2\end{aligned}$
Translational kinetic energy $E_r=\frac{1}{2} m v^2\begin{aligned} \therefore \text { Total energy } & =\frac{1}{5} m v^2+\frac{1}{2} m v^2 \\ & =\frac{7}{10} m v^2\end{aligned}\therefore$ Required fraction $=\frac{\frac{1}{5} m v^2}{\frac{7}{10} m v^2}=\frac{2}{7}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The amplification factor of a triode valve is 15 . If the grid voltage is changed by 0.3 V , the change in plate voltage in order to keep the current constant (in volt) is :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \mu=15, \Delta V_g & =0 \cdot 3 \\ \therefore \quad \mu & =\frac{\Delta V_p}{\Delta V_g} \Rightarrow \Delta V_p=\mu \Delta V_g \\ & =15 \times 0.3 \\ & =4.5 \mathrm{~V} .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two rods of same material have same length and area. The heat $\Delta Q$ flows through them for 12 minutes when they are joint side by side. If now both the rods are joined in parallel, then the same amount of heat $\Delta Q$ will flow in :
questions.solution: When rods are joined in series then heat flow $\begin{aligned} & \Delta Q_1=\frac{A\left(T_1-T_2\right) t_1}{\frac{l_1}{K_1}+\frac{l_1}{K_2}} \\ & =\frac{A\left(T_1-T_2\right) t_1}{\frac{l}{K_1}+\frac{l}{K_2}}=\frac{A\left(T_1-T_2\right) t_1}{l} \frac{K}{2}\end{aligned}$ When rods are joined in parallel $\begin{aligned} \Delta Q_2 & =\left(K_1 A+K_2 A\right) \frac{\left(T_1-T_2\right) t_2}{l} \\ & =\frac{2 K A\left(T_1-T_2\right) t_2}{l} \\ \because \Delta Q_1 & =\Delta Q_2\quad(given)\end{aligned}$ $\therefore \quad t_2=\frac{t_1}{4}=\frac{12}{4}=3 \mathrm{~min}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A perfect gas is found to obey the relation $P V^{3 / 2}=$ constant during an adiabatic process. If such a gas initially at a temperature $T$, is compressed to half of its initial volume, then its final temperature will be :
questions.solution:
Gas obeys the equation
$P V^{3 / 2}=$ constant
Comparing with $P V^\gamma=$ constant
$\gamma=\frac{3}{2}$
For adiabatic process
$\begin{aligned} T_1 V_1^{\gamma-1} & =T_2 V_2^{\gamma-1} \\ T(V)^{3 / 2-1} & =T_2\left(\frac{V}{2}\right)^{3 / 2-1} \\ T_2 & =T(2)^{3 / 2-1} \\ & =(2)^{1 / 2} T\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In isothermal process, which of the following is not true?
options: No heat enters or leaves the system
questions.solution: In isothermal process, heat enters or leaves the system, to keep the temperature constant, so statement (c) is wrong.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force $F$ is given by $F=a t+b t^2$, where, $t$ is time. What are the dimensions of $a$ and $b$ ?
questions.solution:
Force $F=a t+b t^2$
From principle of homogeneity, Dimensions of $a t=$ dimensions of $F\therefore$ Dimensions of $a=\frac{[F]}{[t]}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right]}{[\mathrm{T}]}=\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-3}\right]$
Similarly, dimensions of
$b=\frac{[F]}{\left[t^2\right]}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{T}^2\right]}=\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-4}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a system of units if force $(F)$, acceleration $(A)$, and time ( $T$ ) are taken as fundamental units, then the dimensional formula of energy is :
questions.solution:
Let energy $E=F^x A^y T^3$
Writing the dimensions on both sides
$\begin{aligned} & {\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]=\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right]^x\left[\mathrm{LT}^{-2}\right]^y[\mathrm{~T}]^2} \\ & {\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]=\left[\mathrm{M}^x \mathrm{~L}^{x+y} \mathrm{~T}^{-2 x-2 y+z}\right]}\end{aligned}$
On comparing both sides
$\begin{aligned} & x=1 \\ & x+y=2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y=2-x=2-1=1 \\ & \text { and } \quad-2 x-2 y+z=-2 \\ & \Rightarrow-2 \times 1-2 \times 1+z=-2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad z=-2+2+2 \\ & =2 \\ & \end{aligned}\therefore$ Dimensional formula of energy
$=F A T^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: There are 26 tuning forks arranged in the decreasing order of their frequencies. Each tuning fork gives 3 beats with the next. The first one is octave of the last. What is the frequency of 18 th tuning fork?
questions.solution:
Each tuning forck gives 3 beats with the next, so the difference in the frequencies of two consecutive forks is 3 .
$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad f_{26} & =f_1+(n-1) \times-3 \\ f & =2 f+(26-1) \times-3 \\ f & =75 \mathrm{~Hz} .\end{aligned}\therefore$ Frequency of 18 th tuning fork
$\begin{aligned} f_{18} & =f_1+(18-1) \times-3 \\ & =2 \times 75+17 \times-3 \\ & =150-51=99 \mathrm{~Hz}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person is observing two trains one coming towards him and other leaving with the same velocity $4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If their whistling frequencies are 240 Hz each, then the number of beats per second heard by the person will be : (if velocity of sound is $320 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ )
questions.solution:
Observed frequency of first train
$\begin{aligned} n_1 & =\frac{v}{v-v_s} \times n \\ & =\frac{320}{320-4} \times 240 \\ & =\frac{320}{316} \times 240 \\ & =243 \mathrm{~Hz} .\end{aligned}$
Observed frequency of second train
$\begin{aligned} n_2 & =\frac{v}{v+v_s} n \\ & =\frac{320}{320+4} \times 240 \\ & =237 \mathrm{~Hz} .\end{aligned}\therefore$ Number of beats $=243-237=6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The equation of stationary wave along a stretched string is given by $y=5 \sin \frac{\pi x}{3} \cos 40 \pi t$, where, $x$ and $y$ are in cm and $t$ in second. The separation between two adjacent nodes is :

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which is gonadotropin hormone?
questions.solution:
Gonadotropins or gonadotropic hormones are as follows.
(a) Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) : It stimulates growth of ovarian follicles and their secretion of oestrogen in the female and spermatogenesis in the male.
(b) Interstitial Cell Stimulating Hormone (ICSH) : It activates the Leydig's cells of the testis to secrete androgens. In female it stimulates the corpus luteum of the ovary to secrete progesterone. In female ICSH is termed as LH (Luteinizing Hormone).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following hormone stimulates the gastric secretion?
questions.solution:
Gastrin hormone is secreted by the the gastric glands to release the gastric juice. Enterogasterone is secreted by the duodenal epithelium. It inhibits the secretion of gastric juice and slows gastric contraction.
Cholecystokinin pancreozymin (CCK-PZ) is secreted by entire small intestine. It stimulates the gall bladder to release bile and the pancreas to release enzymes in the pancreatic juice.
Villikinin accelerates the movement of intestinal villi.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: 'Digestion' word means :
questions.solution: Digestion is a process in which non-diffusible foods are converted into diffusible foods with the help of digestive enzymes. Digestion is mostly carried out by the process of hydrolysis using water molecules for the cleavage. The enzymes which bring about digestion are called hydrolases.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Maximum absorption of water occurs in :
questions.solution: The chief functions of the large intestine are the absorption of water and the elimination of solid wastes. Large intestine is divided into three parts i.e., caecum, colon and rectum. In mammals, colon has essential water absorbing role in preparation of faeces.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During starvation what will be sequence of ending of food stuffs ?
questions.solution:
During starvation reserve carbohydrate is used up firstly by the body and after carbohydrates, fat is used as energy source and at last, when both carbohydrate and fat are absent, proteins are used as energy source. Therefore, the sequence is
Carbohydrate \rightarrow  Fat \rightarrow  Protein

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which have not left any evidences of organic evolution?
questions.solution:
The organisms which possess the characters of two different groups are called connecting links. They provide the evidence of organic evolution.
Examples :
(1) Archaeopteryx is connecting link between reptiles and birds.
(2) Neopilina is connecting link between Annelida and Mollusca.
(3) Peripatus is connecting link between Annelida and Arthropoda.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Set which includes only analogous organs is :
options: wings of butterfly, housefly and bat
hindlegs of horse, grasshopper and bat
wings of butterfly and wingspread of bat and birds
mandibles of cockroach, mosquito and honey bee
questions.solution:
Analogous organs have similar functions but are different in their structure and origin.
Examples :
(1) Wings of butterfly, birds and bat have similar functions.
(2) Stings of honey bee and scorpion are analogous structures.
(3) Fins of fishes and flippers of whales are analogous organs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Organs which differ in origin but perform similar functions :
questions.solution:
The organs which have similar function but are different in their structure and origin are called analogous organs.
The organs which have same fundamental structure and origin but function may be similar or different, are called homologous organs.
The organs which are present in reduced form and do not correspond to the fully developed functional organs to related animals are called vestigial organs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: 'Convergent Evolution' is shown by :
questions.solution: Convergent evolution or adaptive convergence or parallel evolution is shown by analogous organs, whereas divergent evolution or evolutionary divergence or adaptive radiation are shown by homologous organs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Example of analogous organs is :
questions.solution: Wings of bird and insects are analogous organs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Lathyrism is caused by :
questions.solution: Lathyrism is caused due to consumption of khesari dal (Lathyrus odoratus).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: How many sperms are formed by four primary spermatocytes ?
questions.solution: Spermatogenesis is the formation of sperm from a germ cell. Four spermatozoa are produced from a primary spermatocyte, therefore, 16 spermatozoa will be formed from four primary spermatocytes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Acrosome is formed by :
questions.solution: Acrosome is the penetrating tip of spermatozoan which is formed of Golgi apparatus. It contains hyaluronidase and several lytic enzymes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Lactic acid is produced by Rhizopus species :
questions.solution:
Rhizopus species causing fermentation are :
(i) R. oryzae - Alcoholic fermentation
(ii) R. nodosus - Lactic acid fermentation
(iii) R. stolonifer (R. nigricans) - Fumaric acid fermentation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Sequence of DNA (non-coding) is known as :
questions.solution: Introns are DNA sequence lying within a coding sequence (exons) but not usually encoding cell product and resulting so called split genes. Cistron is a segment of linear DNA encoding a specific and functional product, usually protein.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which is called soluble RNA ?
questions.solution:
There are following three types of cellular RNA.
(1) Transfer RNA or soluble RNA
(2) Messenger RNA or template RNA
(3) Ribosomal RNA
Transfer RNA ( $t$-RNA) and messenger RNA (m-RNA) are synthesized on DNA template of chromosomes while ribosomal RNA ( $r$-RNA) is derived from nucleolar DNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Non-genetic RNA is of :
questions.solution:
Non-genetic RNA is found in all eukaryotic and prokaryotic organisms. It is of three types i.e.,
(i) Ribosomal RNA ( $r$-RNA)
(ii) Transfer RNA ( $t$-RNA)
(iii) Messenger RNA (m-RNA)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Transformation in bacteria was discovered by :
questions.solution: Griffiths (1928), for the first time, reported transformation in bacteria and later on Avery, Mcleod and McCarthy (1944) studied it in detail.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: On high mountains, difficulty in breathing is due to :
questions.solution: in partial pressure.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Biotic factors are :
options: chemical factors of soil which affect life
physical factors of soil which affect life
all living organisms which influence other organisms
factors of atmosphere which affect life
questions.solution: Biotic factors include all the living organisms which influence the other organisms.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The arrangement of genes on chromosomes in :
questions.solution: According to chromosome theory, proposed by Morgan and Castle (1912), the genes showing linkage are situated on the same pair of chromosome and are arranged in a linear fashion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Kappa particles indicate :
questions.solution: Kappa particles are found in Paramecium and possess cytoplasmic inheritance, also called extra-chromosomal inheritance.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Chloragogen cells help in :
questions.solution: Chloragogen cells or yellow cells are present in the region of intestine in Pheretima. The exact function of these cells is not fully known but it is believed that they are concerned with storage of reserve food and also excretory in function. Chloragogen cells are analogous to liver of vertebrates.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Chloragogen cells of earthworms are analogous to vertebrate :
questions.solution: Chloragogen cells of earthworm are analogous to liver of vertebrates.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Lymphocytes are formed by :
questions.solution: Lymphocyte is a type of agranular leucocyte formed by lymph gland and lymph node. Mast cells are cells of connective tissue, modified from basophil of blood and secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin. Plasma cells are cells of connective tissue, which synthesize antibodies.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Number of cranial nerves in frog :
questions.solution: Ten pairs of cranial nerves are present in anamniotes such as fishes and amphibians (e.g., Frog). Twelve pairs of cranial nerves are present in amniotes, reptiles, birds and mammals including rabbit and humans.
